designPrinciple: A beginner first sees a bounded explanation or demonstration, predicts and traces behavior, then writes, breaks, repairs, tests, explains, and proves a progressively less scaffolded program.
targetLearner: A tertiary fresher or independent beginner with basic computer literacy and no assumed programming experience
technologySequence: CLI integration, Git, README, and GitHub
learningRhythm: required Build in sessions of at most two hours

resourceRoleStrategy.learn: A short first explanation or demonstration.
resourceRoleStrategy.practice: An observable prediction, trace, or action.
resourceRoleStrategy.reference: A precise bounded lookup used beside immediate work, never an unscoped documentation dump.

progressionPolicy: Weeks 4–6 combine earlier syntax in distinct small programs.
Week 8 integrates earlier competencies into one larger independently inspectable project.
workloadPrinciples: Eight instructional Weeks at six hours each.
Setup is separate and skippable only through explicit verification.
Most time is reserved for coding, debugging, tests, evidence, and explanation rather than passive consumption.
assessmentPolicy: Each Week has ten independently authored, source-mapped questions; 7/10 passes; attempts are unlimited; option order reshuffles per attempt; code and project competence is judged through Build and Proof, not quiz score alone.

projectArchitecture.title: JavaScript Practice Portfolio
projectArchitecture.outcome: Produce seven progressively stronger programs demonstrating execution, values, decisions, collections, functions, structured data, persistence, tests, and debugging.

projectArchitecture.title: FoundIt CLI
projectArchitecture.outcome: Deliver and publish a tested, persistent lost-and-found command-line program with a reproducible README and human-reviewable evidence.
